analysis:
Examined both added files, their metadata, complete patches and numbered source. The workflow introduces scheduled repository-wide cancellation/rerun authority using actions:write and checks:write (.github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml:21–40). It executes fixed shell code without checkout or evaluation of job-provided text; API credentials are sent to the GitHub context's HTTPS endpoint without redirect following (90–101). Job names are sanitized before logging, and JSON arguments are passed through jq (145–149, 268–271). Candidate selection requires aged, unassigned Darkbloom-labelled jobs; mutation checks the current attempt and limits normal rescues (228–262). No directly supported credential disclosure or execution-injection regression was identified.

The canonical index concerns provider/runtime boundaries; this CI watchdog is distinct from the local rollback watchdog in T-043. No supplied change alters A-001/A-003 encryption, T-041 cache isolation, App Attest authorization (T-052–T-058), fan authority, or add-on execution. The new CI token and cross-branch rerun authority warrant separate threat-model coverage, especially if rerunnable workflows publish qualified artifacts (A-011/A-017); that interaction is not established here.

Integration must verify the route workflow's promised fallback behavior against rerun selection at lines 155–176 and the changelog's activation claim (changelog.d/ci-darkbloom-watchdog-on-master.md:3). Also examine marker ownership: recovery accepts github-actions markers (202–204), while earlier-attempt detection accepts markers from any app (249–251). Supplied evidence does not establish an attacker with check-writing access, so marker spoofing is not reported as a vulnerability. Mark-before-cancel recovery (265–282) can also resume a cancellation performed concurrently by another actor; integration should establish intended operator-cancellation semantics and downstream rerun side effects. These missing interactions limit conclusions rather than prove a regression.
